edits.previous: In native PHP packages, a Lean `Fin n` parameter or result is a `Brick\Math\BigInteger`, the same as `Nat`. For `Library.mirror (value : Fin 10) : Fin 10`, `mirror(BigInteger::of(3))` returns 6. `mirror(BigInteger::of(10))` throws `LeanBridgeError` with code 1 and the message `arg0 is not below its Fin 10 bound`. A negative value throws `ValueError` and a non-BigInteger argument throws `TypeError`, as they do for `Nat`. The package checks the bound before it calls Lean, so caller data is unchanged and a later valid call still works. `Fin 0` parameters reject every value, and bounds wider than 64 bits are compared exactly. PHPDoc on each function and the package README state the bound. Top-level parameters and results are supported, including inside `Array`, `List` and `Option` (for example `Array (Fin 10)` or `Option (List (Fin 10))`): every element is checked before Lean is called, an empty array or `none` is valid even for `Fin 0`, and a rejection names the parameter and the bound of the element that failed. Fields, callbacks, products and results are not; see the [installed checks](evidence/native-fin-hosts-20261006.md) and the [container checks](evidence/native-fin-containers-20261006.md).

Native PHP generates Fin checks in pairs, Except and fields, but their installed acceptance is not recorded; Fin in callbacks is rejected.

### Bounded integers in PHP-Wasm

PHP-Wasm plain copied packages also preserve `Fin` bounds in pairs, active
`Except` branches, copied record/variant fields and their tested `Array`, `List`
and `Option` combinations. Use `Brick\Math\BigInteger`, including for bounds
wider than 64 bits. `none` is valid for `Option (Fin 0)`;
a present `Fin 0` value is rejected. Both weak and strict callers retain their
input values and can call the package again after a rejection.

The [ordinary](evidence/php-wasm-fin-20261008/receipt.json) and
[reviewed](evidence/reviewed-php-wasm-fin-20261008/receipt.json) package tests
each execute 11 product exports and 13 record/variant exports. Every fixture
runs in eight Node configurations (embedded or Composer, startup or lazy,
weak or strict) and four Chromium bundled configurations. These runs use
Node 22.23.3, Chromium 154.0.8037.57, PHP 8.4.1 and php-wasm 0.1.0.
These fixtures do not execute bare top-level `Fin` or direct
`Array (Fin n)`, `List (Fin n)` or `Option (Fin n)` exports.
Source-dispatch counters were not measured. PHP-Wasm checked `Subtype`,
refined callbacks and refinements combined with graph or owned transports
remain unsupported.
